scope: Read-only search for visual reference candidates for Oxyrhynchus/El-Bahnasa and Roman Mediolanum. File pages and stated licenses inspected; no image downloaded. These are candidates for architectural review, not approved production assets.

candidates.asset: Karte Oxyrhynchos.png (locator map of ancient Oxyrhynchus in Egypt)
candidates.author: NordNordWest; source credited as earlier Oxyrhynchos map.gif by Yomangani
candidates.license: Public domain uploader dedication (PD-self); not identified as CC0
candidates.sourceInspected: Commons summary, authorship/source, and public-domain license sections read directly.
candidates.visualScope: Small locator map only; locates Oxyrhynchus in Egypt, not ancient street plan or local terrain.
candidates.phaseAndAnachronism: Modern orientation map, not an archaeological plan or period city image. Use only as geographic locator, and do not style it as a 3rd-century reconstruction.
candidates.status: license explicit; low-resolution locator reference only; productionApproved:false

candidates.asset: Osireion Oxyrhynchus.jpg (gallery of the subterranean Osireion)
candidates.author: Bombaladan
candidates.license: CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported; attribution and share-alike required
candidates.sourceInspected: Commons image page inspected: author, own-work claim, dimensions, exact license. For monument phase, Oxyrhynchus Archaeological Mission page was directly opened: it says inscriptions date rites from Ptolemy VI to Ptolemy X/Cleopatra III (second half of 2nd c. BCE), says Per-Khef existed in Saite period and was restored under early Ptolemies; the wall page says surviving underground fabric is basically Ptolemaic. UB thesis record title bounds ritual study c. 7th century BCE–2nd century CE.
candidates.visualScope: Actual excavated underground Osireion gallery, not a panorama of the Roman-period city.
candidates.phaseAndAnachronism: Primarily Ptolemaic monument (surviving subterranean fabric), with use/ritual chronology extending into Roman period in the cited study. It can serve as a specifically labelled cult-site reference only; it must not stand for ordinary 250 CE streets, a Christian church, or the city center. Site page is mission material; phase claim is summarized there, not independent stratigraphic report read in full.
candidates.status: license explicit; archaeological monument candidate with strong phase caveat; productionApproved:false

candidates.asset: UCL Digital Egypt plan of Oxyrhynchus following Petrie / Greenfield and Hunt
candidates.author: Historical plan by Petrie, with orientation corrections according to Greenfield and Hunt; UCL page presents it
candidates.date: Underlying excavation plans published in 1925; institutional web page © UCL 2003
candidates.license: No open license identified; page states © University College London, all rights reserved
candidates.sourceInspected: The page text and copyright line read. It says the plan follows Petrie 1925 pl. XXXIX and includes orientation corrections from Greenfield and Hunt.
candidates.visualScope: Potentially useful site plan depicting theatre, colonnade and broader site; not itself a modern free-use file.
candidates.phaseAndAnachronism: Plan is a composite of early 20th-century survey interpretations, not a dated single-phase plan. UCL notes orientation correction; elsewhere on the site it cautions that the colonnade's function remains uncertain and that ‘temple’ on the early draft was actually Petrie's theatre. No reuse without separate permission or a demonstrably public-domain scan/source.
candidates.status: not a reusable open-license candidate; excluded pending rights evidence; productionApproved:false

candidates.asset: Mediolanum Romana.svg (schematic map of Roman Milan)
candidates.author: Original: Cristiano64; vectorization: MacMoreno; current file amended by Arrow303
candidates.license: Dual license: CC BY-SA 3.0 Unported or GFDL 1.2+ (page says user may choose); attribution/share-alike conditions apply under CC option
candidates.sourceInspected: Commons summary/history and exact licensing section inspected. Page describes features and period as 3rd–5th centuries CE: walls/gates, forum, theater, amphitheater, circus, imperial-palace area, mint, baths, mausoleum, portico road, horrea, river port, early Christian basilicas.
candidates.visualScope: Retrospective schematic ancient-city layout superimposed/organized as a city plan; includes structures of multiple centuries.
candidates.phaseAndAnachronism: Time span III–V c. combines different building phases, so it is not a verified 313 snapshot. In particular do not assume every labeled basilica or imperial complex existed at the episode date, or use shown outlines as excavation-grade coordinates. This is a community-created map with no archaeological bibliography apparent in the consulted page; useful as a lead/reference only. Not a cathedral photo.
candidates.status: license explicit; secondary schematic requiring phase validation; productionApproved:false

candidates.asset: Basamento circo.jpg (surviving remains of Roman circus)
candidates.author: Zanner
candidates.license: Public domain uploader dedication (PD-self); not identified as CC0
candidates.sourceInspected: Commons page inspected for description, author, original date, file dimensions, and public-domain grant.
candidates.visualScope: Modern photograph of surviving archaeological remains / base associated with the Roman circus, not a period reconstruction.
candidates.phaseAndAnachronism: Photograph shows a surviving, much-altered fragment in present-day Milan; no precise construction or exposure date for the photographed masonry is established by the file page. Can be a material reference, not a 4th-century intact circus reconstruction or exact phase claim.
candidates.status: license explicit; archaeological-remains photo candidate; productionApproved:false

candidates.asset: Torre della cinta muraria di Mediolanum.jpg (Roman wall tower preserved within Archaeological Museum)
candidates.author: Ugodiamante
candidates.license: CC BY-SA 4.0 International; attribution and share-alike required
candidates.sourceInspected: Commons file page directly inspected for monument description, creator/date, coordinates of photo, and license.
candidates.visualScope: Photo of a standing remnant/tower of the Roman wall at the Civic Archaeological Museum; contemporary museum context visible/implicit.
candidates.phaseAndAnachronism: The image is a modern museum-preserved remnant, not a reconstructed intact wall or an exact street-level view of 313 Milan. Page does not provide the wall/tower's precise construction date or phase; avoid treating whole fortification as a unitary construction episode.

candidates.author: Pierangelo66
candidates.license: Commons page grants CC BY-SA 3.0 but also states separate Italian cultural-heritage authorization is required for reuse beyond personal use/study, especially commercial reuse
candidates.licenseUrl: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/ ; Italian Code of Cultural Heritage disclaimer is on file page
candidates.sourceInspected: Commons file page inspected, including author/date, exact CC license and Italian MiBAC/Codice Urbani additional-authorization disclaimer.
candidates.visualScope: Modern archaeological park with scant foundations of the amphitheatre; Commons category description says most building stone was reused/demolished in antiquity.
candidates.phaseAndAnachronism: Clearly not a view of an intact ancient amphitheatre; source says only short foundation row survives and demolition/reuse occurred during antiquity. Despite the CC license, additional heritage authorization disclaimer makes it a poor candidate for distribution without permission. Do not use as 313 architecture reconstruction.
candidates.status: not recommended without additional authorization; productionApproved:false

candidates.asset: The Ancient Urban Form of Mediolanum Superimposed Over Milan.png
candidates.author: Kdonavin
candidates.sourceInspected: Commons page inspected for author, date, explicit CC0 dedication and caption.
candidates.visualScope: Map placing ancient urban form over a modern Milan base.
candidates.phaseAndAnachronism: Very recent user-created work, not institutional archaeology; consulted page supplies no bibliography or method for boundaries/features. Useful only to orient further research, not as factual layout or a chronology. Production caution especially high notwithstanding open license.
candidates.status: license explicit; unvalidated secondary map; not recommended as authoritative reference; productionApproved:false

institutionalCrossChecks.consultedScope: Oxford Oxyrhynchus Papyri site page read for survey plans, ancient theatre/colonnade, Bahr Yussuf, modern/islamic features; page explicitly says the Bahr Yussuf is a natural Nile branch, distinguishes late 9th/15th/18th-century monuments, and notes uncertain function of colonnade. Page copyright does not grant open reuse for displayed photos/plans.
Osireion and wall pages directly read. Mission dates textual attestation to Saite period and restoration under early Ptolemies; wall page dates surviving subterranean part broadly to Ptolemaic.
University of Barcelona thesis record: title bounds study of Osireion rituals to c. 7th century BCE–2nd century CE; abstract/record only.
Museum of Milan page search excerpt describes Roman museum content (including mosaics from domus); direct opening returned 403, so not considered fully read.

generalNotes: No candidate is approved for production; architects should inspect crops/context and ensure chosen asset fits the episode year.
A modern photo of an ancient site documents present remains, not necessarily the ancient phase; the mapping and phase limitations above are material.
Milan cathedral photographs were not selected or used.
